messages.content:
You are a senior logistics optimization consultant. Analyze the following supply chain problem and provide a comprehensive solution.

IMPORTANT: This is a unique benchmark test with timestamp {{TIMESTAMP}}. Do NOT use any cached responses - generate fresh analysis.

A manufacturing company operates 5 factories (A, B, C, D, E) producing 3 product lines (X, Y, Z). Each factory has different production capabilities and costs:

Factory A: Can produce X and Y. Production cost: X=$120/unit, Y=$180/unit. Max capacity: 10,000 units/day.
Factory B: Can produce Y and Z. Production cost: Y=$150/unit, Z=$200/unit. Max capacity: 8,000 units/day.
Factory C: Can produce X, Y, and Z. Production cost: X=$110/unit, Y=$170/unit, Z=$190/unit. Max capacity: 12,000 units/day.
Factory D: Can produce X and Z. Production cost: X=$125/unit, Z=$210/unit. Max capacity: 9,000 units/day.
Factory E: Can produce Y and Z. Production cost: Y=$160/unit, Z=$195/unit. Max capacity: 7,000 units/day.

Demand requirements (daily):
- Product X: 8,000 units minimum
- Product Y: 10,000 units minimum
- Product Z: 6,000 units minimum

Shipping costs per unit to 3 distribution centers:
- From Factory A: $15 to DC1, $20 to DC2, $25 to DC3
- From Factory B: $18 to DC1, $16 to DC2, $22 to DC3
- From Factory C: $12 to DC1, $19 to DC2, $21 to DC3
- From Factory D: $20 to DC1, $17 to DC2, $18 to DC3
- From Factory E: $22 to DC1, $21 to DC2, $15 to DC3

Distribution center requirements (daily):
- DC1: 7,000 units minimum
- DC2: 8,000 units minimum
- DC3: 5,000 units minimum

Constraints:
1. Each factory must maintain at least 20% of its capacity on its most expensive product line
2. No single factory can supply more than 40% of any single distribution center
3. Factory C must produce at least one unit of each product line
4. The ratio of X:Y:Z production across all factories must be within 35%:45%:20% +/-5%
5. Total daily shipping cost must not exceed $500,000

Provide:
1. An optimal production plan (units per product per factory)
2. Distribution plan (units from each factory to each DC)
3. Total daily production cost
4. Total daily shipping cost
5. Total daily cost (production + shipping)
6. Identify any bottlenecks
7. Suggest one improvement that would reduce costs by at least 5%

Show your work step by step, including the mathematical formulation of the optimization problem.

messages.content:
Analyze the following comprehensive technical specification document and provide a detailed summary with architectural recommendations.

IMPORTANT: This is a unique benchmark test with timestamp {{TIMESTAMP}}. Do NOT use any cached responses - generate fresh analysis.

=== Technical Specification: Enterprise Microservices Platform v4.0 ===

1. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
1.1 Purpose
This document outlines the technical specifications for the next-generation enterprise microservices platform, codenamed Aurora. The platform is designed to support 10,000+ concurrent API endpoints, process 1 million+ transactions per second, and maintain 99.999% availability across three geographic regions.

1.2 Scope
The Aurora platform replaces the legacy monolithic application (codenamed Titan) which currently processes 500K transactions/second across 2,000 API endpoints. The migration must be completed within 18 months with zero downtime.

2. ARCHITECTURE OVERVIEW
2.1 Service Mesh
- Primary: Istio 1.19+ with Envoy proxy
- Secondary: Linkerd for low-latency services
- mTLS: Automatic certificate rotation every 24 hours
- Traffic splitting: Canary deployments with 5% baseline traffic

2.2 API Gateway
- Kong Gateway 3.4 with custom plugins
- Rate limiting: Token bucket algorithm, 10K req/s per tenant
- Authentication: OAuth 2.0 + OIDC with JWKS rotation
- Request transformation: gRPC to REST, GraphQL federation

2.3 Data Layer
- Primary: PostgreSQL 16 (sharded, 12 nodes)
- Cache: Redis 7.2 cluster (256 GB total, 16 nodes)
- Search: Elasticsearch 8.11 (3 data nodes, 2 master nodes)
- Time-series: TimescaleDB 2.14 (5 nodes, 100TB capacity)
- Object storage: MinIO (4 nodes, 1PB raw storage)

2.4 Message Queue
- Primary: Apache Kafka 3.6 (9 brokers, 64 partitions per topic)
- Dead letter: Separate Kafka cluster for error handling
- Stream processing: Apache Flink 1.18 (32 task managers)

3. SECURITY REQUIREMENTS
3.1 Authentication
- Multi-factor: TOTP + hardware keys (FIDO2)
- Service accounts: SPIFFE/SPIRE with short-lived JWTs
- User provisioning: SCIM 2.0 with Azure AD sync
- Session management: JWT with 15-minute expiry, refresh tokens 7 days

3.2 Authorization
- RBAC: 50+ roles, hierarchical permissions
- ABAC: Attribute-based policies for data-level access
- PDP: OPA 0.64 with Rego policies
- Audit: All access decisions logged to immutable storage

3.3 Encryption
- At rest: AES-256-GCM with per-tenant keys (AWS KMS)
- In transit: TLS 1.3 everywhere, HSTS with preload
- Database: TDE with column-level encryption for PII
- Secrets: HashiCorp Vault with automatic rotation

3.4 Compliance
- SOC 2 Type II (annual audit)
- PCI DSS Level 1 (payment processing)
- GDPR: Right to erasure, data portability
- HIPAA: PHI protection for health data

4. MONITORING AND OBSERVABILITY
4.1 Metrics
- Prometheus 3.0 (3 replicas, 14-day retention)
- Grafana 10.4 (50+ dashboards, 200+ alerts)
- Custom metrics: OpenTelemetry SDK, 100K+ unique metric series

4.2 Logging
- ELK stack: 50TB/day ingestion
- Structured logging: JSON with correlation IDs
- Log retention: 90 days hot, 1 year warm, 7 years cold (compliance)
- PII filtering: Automatic redaction at ingestion

4.3 Tracing
- Jaeger/Tempo hybrid: 10% sampling rate, 100M spans/day
- Service dependency map: Auto-discovered via service mesh
- P99 latency tracking: Per-service, per-endpoint, per-region

4.4 Alerting
- PagerDuty integration: 200+ alert rules
- Escalation: 3 levels, 5-minute intervals
- On-call: Rotation with Slack integration
- Incident response: Automated runbooks for 50+ scenarios

5. CI/CD PIPELINE
5.1 Build
- GitHub Actions: 100 concurrent runners
- Container: Docker BuildKit, multi-stage builds
- SBOM: CycloneDX, SPDX compliance
- Signing: Cosign with keyless signing (OIDC)

5.2 Testing
- Unit: pytest (Python), JUnit5 (Java), Jest (TypeScript)
- Integration: Testcontainers, 500+ test suites
- E2E: Playwright, 200 test scenarios
- Performance: k6, 50 load test scenarios
- Security: Trivy, Semgrep, SonarQube

5.3 Deployment
- GitOps: ArgoCD with sync waves
- Strategy: Blue-green for critical services, canary for others
- Rollback: Automatic on error rate > 1%
- Environment: Dev (3 nodes), Staging (6 nodes), Prod (18 nodes)

6. DISASTER RECOVERY
6.1 Backup
- Frequency: Incremental every 5 minutes, full daily
- Retention: 35 days (compliance requirement)
- Encryption: AES-256 at rest, TLS in transit
- Testing: Monthly restore drills, 15-minute RTO target

6.2 Failover
- Active-Active: Three regions (us-east-1, eu-west-1, ap-southeast-1)
- RPO: less than 1 second (synchronous replication)
- RTO: less than 5 minutes (automated failover)
- DNS: Route53 latency-based routing with health checks

7. PERFORMANCE TARGETS
7.1 Latency
- P50: less than 50ms (API Gateway)
- P95: less than 200ms
- P99: less than 500ms
- Database: P99 less than 10ms (read), less than 50ms (write)

7.2 Throughput
- API Gateway: 1M req/s sustained
- Database: 500K writes/s, 2M reads/s
- Message queue: 100K events/s per topic

7.3 Scalability
- Horizontal: Auto-scale based on CPU (70% threshold)
- Vertical: Up to 64 vCPU, 256GB RAM per pod
- Karpenter: Node provisioning in less than 10 seconds

8. COST ESTIMATES
8.1 Infrastructure (Monthly)
- Compute: $120,000 (EC2, EKS)
- Database: $45,000 (RDS, ElastiCache, DocumentDB)
- Network: $25,000 (data transfer, load balancers, NAT)
- Storage: $15,000 (EBS, S3, ECR)
- Monitoring: $10,000 (Datadog, PagerDuty)
- Total: $215,000/month

8.2 Cost Optimization Targets
- Year 1: $215,000/month
- Year 2: $180,000/month (-16%)
- Year 3: $150,000/month (-30% from baseline)

After analyzing this document, provide:

1. A 2-paragraph executive summary (50-75 words)
2. A detailed architecture assessment covering:
   - Strengths of the proposed architecture
   - Potential single points of failure
   - Security gaps or concerns
   - Performance bottleneck risks
3. A migration plan from Titan to Aurora with:
   - Phase breakdown (min 5 phases)
   - Risk assessment per phase
   - Rollback strategy
   - Timeline estimation
4. A cost-benefit analysis comparing the old vs new system
5. A prioritized list of 10 technical risks with mitigation strategies
6. Recommendations for 3 areas where the spec could be improved
7. An assessment of whether the 18-month timeline is realistic

Format your response with clear headings, bullet points, and tables where appropriate. Include specific metrics and numbers from the document in your analysis.

I am building a financial analysis dashboard. First, can you help me design the database schema for tracking stock portfolio performance?

IMPORTANT: This is benchmark test run #{{RUN_ID}} at {{TIMESTAMP}}. Do NOT use any cached responses - generate fresh analysis.

I need to track: users, portfolios, holdings, transactions, and price history. Consider that each user can have multiple portfolios, each holding can have multiple transactions over time, and price history needs to support minute-level granularity for trading data.

Additionally, the system must handle:
- Real-time P&L calculations
- Historical performance reporting (YTD, 1M, 3M, 6M, 1Y, 3Y, 5Y)
- Dividend tracking and reinvestment
- Tax-lot accounting for lots acquired at different times
- Integration with 3 external brokerages via CSV import
- Support for crypto assets (BTC, ETH) alongside traditional equities

Provide a complete schema design with all tables, columns, data types, indexes, and foreign keys.

messages.content:
Write production-ready Python code for a real-time stock market data processing pipeline. This is a unique benchmark test with timestamp {{TIMESTAMP}}.

IMPORTANT: Do NOT use any cached responses - generate fresh code.

The system must:

1. Ingest stock tick data via WebSocket from a hypothetical MarketDataAPI
2. Implement a ring buffer for high-frequency price updates (target: 100K messages/second)
3. Calculate rolling statistics (mean, std, min, max) with configurable windows (1s, 5s, 1m, 5m, 1h)
4. Detect anomalies using z-score (threshold: 3.0) and flag them
5. Persist processed data to PostgreSQL with proper connection pooling
6. Expose a REST API (FastAPI) for querying historical data
7. Implement proper error handling, retries with exponential backoff
8. Add comprehensive logging with structured JSON format
9. Include unit tests for the core calculation engine
10. Add Docker Compose for easy deployment

Requirements:
- Use asyncio for all I/O operations
- Implement circuit breaker pattern for the WebSocket connection
- Use SQLAlchemy 2.0 async for database operations
- Include health check endpoints
- Add Prometheus metrics for monitoring
- Implement graceful shutdown

Please provide:
1. The main application entry point
2. The WebSocket client with reconnection logic
3. The ring buffer implementation
4. The statistics calculator
5. The anomaly detector
6. The database models and repository
7. The FastAPI routes
8. The Docker Compose configuration
9. Requirements file
10. Unit tests

Make sure the code is well-documented with docstrings and type hints. Follow PEP 8 style guide.

prompts.title: Creative Technical Writing
prompts.description: Generate creative technical content with specific constraints

messages.content:
Write a comprehensive technical blog post (2000-2500 words) about The Evolution of Database Systems: From Relational to Multi-Model.

IMPORTANT: This is benchmark test run #{{RUN_ID}} at {{TIMESTAMP}}. Do NOT use any cached responses - generate fresh content.

Requirements:
1. Start with a compelling hook - perhaps a historical anecdote about the Y2K problem and how it shaped database choices
2. Cover these eras in detail:
   - The Relational Era (1970s-2000s): SQL, ACID, normalization
   - The NoSQL Revolution (2000s-2010s): CAP theorem, eventual consistency, scaling challenges
   - The Polyglot Persistence Era (2010s-2020s): Document, graph, time-series, vector databases
   - The Multi-Model Era (2020s-present): Combining strengths, HTAP databases
3. Include specific real-world examples (companies, products, benchmarks)
4. Address common misconceptions in each era
5. Provide a decision framework for choosing the right database for a given use case
6. Include a comparison table (markdown format) covering: SQL, MongoDB, Neo4j, InfluxDB, Pinecone, Cassandra
7. End with predictions for the next 5 years
8. Use a conversational yet authoritative tone
9. Include code snippets showing how the same query looks in 3 different database systems
10. Add a Lessons Learned section with 5 key takeaways

The audience is senior software engineers and architects who need to make database decisions.
